evals.name: appointments-from-stories
evals.prompt: We're starting appointments (CLN-41). Can you design the data model for it from the PRD and backlog? Tables, indexes, what's PII and how long we keep it, and the migrations we'd need. Don't write the migrations yet, just the design.
evals.expected_output: A data model design under docs/ that builds on the existing tenants, patients and doctors tables (bigint ids) with tenant-safe references, prevents overlapping appointments of different lengths at the database level, gives each story's query an index with the day view bounded in the clinic's time zone, moves a pending reminder's queue time when its appointment moves and stops it on cancel, adds the doctor's default fee to doctors through a new migration and does not assume one currency for clinics in three countries, keeps the 7 year rule and sizes the table from it, makes the 7 year purge take reminders with it, keeps appointments when a patient asks for erasure, leaves unstated retention open, leaves the phase 2 waitlist out, and plans migrations from 0003 without writing them or recording decisions the user did not make.
expectations: No file was created under migrations/ and no existing file (migrations/0001_tenants.sql, migrations/0002_patients_doctors.sql, the ADRs, the PRD, the backlog or the code) was changed; every new file is part of the data model design under docs/ (a design document, optionally with companion files such as a schema sketch, data dictionary or diagram), and nothing outside that design (a glossary, an ADR for a choice the user did not make, code) was added

The design references the existing tenants, patients and doctors tables by bigint foreign keys (not uuid, no new patient or doctor tables), and the database itself stops an appointment from referencing a patient or doctor of another tenant: for example composite foreign keys on (tenant_id, patient_id) and (tenant_id, doctor_id) against a UNIQUE (tenant_id, id) added to patients and doctors by a new migration, or a trigger. Single-column foreign keys plus application filtering do not pass

Overlapping appointments for the same doctor are prevented by a database constraint that handles different lengths (for example an EXCLUDE USING gist on doctor_id and a tstzrange of start and end); a unique index on the start time alone does not pass unless the document states that it misses overlaps between 15, 30 and 45 minute appointments, and the rule does not apply to cancelled appointments so a cancelled slot can be booked again as US-05-003 requires

The day view of US-05-001 (one doctor, one day, ordered by start) is served by an index whose leading columns are the tenant or doctor followed by the start time, and the design says the day is bounded in the clinic's own time zone (from tenants.timezone), not a UTC calendar day, since clinics span India, the UAE and Singapore

The reminder sender's query for pending reminders that are due is served by an index (for example a partial index on the send time WHERE status is pending), and the design states how it reads "a failed send is retried up to 3 times" (3 attempts in total, or a first send plus 3 retries), with an attempt limit that matches that reading and the reading raised as a question for the user

The design says what happens to a pending reminder when its appointment is cancelled (it is not sent) and when it is rescheduled (it goes out 24 hours before the new start), and how: on reschedule the column the sender's due-reminder index reads is the one that is reset (if the model has both a due time and a next-attempt time, both move, or the design explains why one suffices)

The appointment fee is a bigint minor units column named with the _minor suffix plus a currency char(3) column (ADR 0002), and US-05-007's per-doctor default fee is modelled on the existing doctors table (for example doctors.default_fee_minor with its currency) through a new migration, not by editing 0002; no float, real or double precision column holds money

The design does not hard-code a single currency such as INR or a 'paise' assumption for every clinic: it takes the currency per clinic or per row, or raises as an open question that ADR 0002's wording (paise) does not fit clinics in the UAE and Singapore
The document gives appointments the 7 year retention from the PRD and names the reason for visit (whatever the column is called) as health-related PII

Retention the PRD does not state (for example reminder delivery data or the phone number a reminder was sent to) is recorded as undefined or an open question for a named owner; no purge job, TTL, partition drop or deletion schedule is specified to enforce a number the PRD does not give. A number offered only as a suggestion inside the open question passes; a number written as the rule or wired into a mechanism does not

The design computes the steady-state size of appointments under the 7 year retention from the PRD volume (about 2.4 million a year kept 7 years, roughly 17 million rows or more with growth) and uses that number for a decision such as the purge mechanism, BRIN or partitioning; quoting the yearly volume alone does not pass

The design makes the 7 year purge of appointments possible with reminders present: the reminder's foreign key to its appointment is ON DELETE CASCADE, or the purge deletes reminders first, and the document says which

The design reconciles the PRD's patient deletion request with the 7 year rule: appointments are kept (the foreign key from appointments to patients is not ON DELETE CASCADE, and hard-deleting a patient with appointments inside the 7 years is refused or replaced by erasing the fields not required to be kept), or the conflict is raised as an open question with that consequence stated; a design that would cascade a patient deletion into appointments does not pass

The migration plan lists the new migrations in order, numbered to follow migrations/0002_patients_doctors.sql (0003 onward) in the repository's goose style, and any change to the existing patients or doctors tables is its own new migration

No ADR and no docs/decisions.md row was written for a technology the repository or the request already settles (for example the database or migration tool already in use), and none for a choice the request does not need (for example an ORM or data access library for a design-only request); any choice the run made without an answer from the user is reported as a decision awaiting the user, not recorded as Accepted

If the design partitions appointments, it states how the no-overlap exclusion constraint survives, since PostgreSQL 16 (ADR 0001) cannot declare an exclusion constraint on a partitioned table; a design that does not partition passes this expectation
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: revise-for-online-booking
evals.prompt: Online booking is going into next sprint, stories US-05-009 and US-05-010 are in the backlog now. Please update the data model for it.
evals.expected_output: docs/design/data-model.md is revised in place as a reviewable change to an approved document: a record of what changed and why naming US-05-009 and US-05-010, a per-tenant case-insensitive unique email for patient accounts that also settles re-registration during the 30 day deletion window, a stated link from a patient account to the patients record that carries the phone the reminder needs, the online booking channel recorded, a source for the NOT NULL fee on an online booking, a hold that blocks the slot, sends no reminder and lapses after 10 minutes on every booking path through a sweeper, trigger or booking-time check (not a now() predicate), lock-safe new migrations 0005 onward for the hot appointments table planned but not written, the applied 0003 and 0004 left untouched, and booking-lld.md left alone but named as stale.
expectations: docs/design/data-model.md was updated in place and no second data model document was created (companion files such as a schema sketch, data dictionary or diagram beside it are allowed); no file was created or changed under migrations/, so 0003 and 0004 are unchanged and the new schema changes are planned, not written, as migrations numbered 0005 onward

The update is reviewable against the approved document: sections the online booking change does not touch keep their content and structure (renumbering a heading to make room for a new section is fine), and the reminders table and its two indexes are unchanged in the design; rewriting the whole document into a new layout or wording does not pass even if the schema it describes is the same
The document or the final message records what changed in this update and why, naming US-05-009 and US-05-010
No reminder is created for a held slot: a reminder row is created only when an appointment is booked or a hold is confirmed, so a lapsed hold never sends an SMS

Patient account email uniqueness is per tenant and case-insensitive (for example a unique index on (tenant_id, lower(email)), citext, or an email stored lower-cased under a CHECK), not unique across all clinics, because US-05-009 allows the same email at different clinics

The patient account email is listed as PII with the 30 day deletion after account closure from US-05-009 and a mechanism that enforces it (for example a scheduled job that deletes or nulls the email), and the design decides what happens when the same email signs up again at the same clinic during those 30 days (for example the unique index covers only open accounts, or the closed account is reopened)

The design states how a patient account relates to the clinic's patients record (for example a patient_id link, one account per patient per clinic) and how a first-time online patient comes to have a patients row, including where its phone number comes from, since appointments.patient_id is NOT NULL and the reminder is sent to patients.phone

The design names where an online booking's fee_minor comes from, since appointments.fee_minor is NOT NULL and US-05-007's per-doctor default fee has no column on doctors: it models the default fee (for example doctors.default_fee_minor through a new migration) or records the missing source as an open question that blocks online booking

Appointments record whether they were booked online (for example a booking channel column or a link to the booking patient account), so the front desk can see which appointments were booked online as US-05-009 requires

A held slot cannot be booked by anyone else, and the database or a stated transactional check enforces it (for example a held status covered by appointments_no_overlap); the hold records when it lapses, 10 minutes after it was taken as US-05-010 says

A lapsed hold does not keep blocking the slot on any booking path, including front desk bookings and reschedules and not only the online confirm: lapsed holds are removed or set to a state the overlap check ignores by a trigger, a sweeper (with the longest time a lapsed hold can still block stated) or a check every booking transaction runs, and the document says which. A design whose only mechanism is a constraint or index predicate that compares with now() does not pass, because PostgreSQL requires those predicates to be immutable

If the design changes the appointments_no_overlap exclusion constraint itself (for example its WHERE clause), it states that an exclusion constraint cannot be built concurrently or added NOT VALID, so recreating it takes an exclusive lock on appointments while its GiST index builds over about 3.1 million rows, and plans for that (a maintenance window, or a design that avoids the change); a design that leaves the constraint as it is passes

Any change to a constraint on the hot appointments table (about 3.1 million rows), such as adding a held status to appointments_status_check, is planned without a validating scan under an exclusive lock, for example ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID followed by VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, or a lock_timeout with the lock risk stated
No table for sign-in codes or passwords is added, since US-05-009 says the auth-gateway service handles them
docs/design/booking-lld.md is left unchanged and named as a document that is now out of date (its status transitions and booking flow do not include the hold); rewriting it unasked does not pass

No ADR, no docs/decisions.md row and no glossary was written for a technology or choice the repository or the request already settles or does not need; any choice the run made without an answer from the user is reported as a decision awaiting the user, not recorded as Accepted
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
